cells.tense: The route is clear right now and the pen is in your hand.
cells.act: build the first new thing from what the clearing showed
cells.ask: Take a spot in your own life that got cleared lately, and build the first true piece of what replaces it, with your hands, before you explain it to anybody.
cells.core:
The crossing is visible to you and you can describe it plainly — turning what you learned the hard way into directions somebody else can follow. A false thing got cleared out, rightly, and you're at the bare ground now, talking through the way across as if it had been there a while.

What you hand around are instructions to a floor you haven't poured. So build the first true piece yourself — a corner, a habit, something that belongs where the old thing stood — with your hands, before the telling. No announcement after. The next instruction carries differently from someone standing on a piece of floor they made.
cells.sheetLine: You can show the crossing. Build one piece of it under yourself.
cells.verb: charting the passage for people who can't yet see the way
cells.place: where you are becoming what you actually are

cells.tense: You are writing the directions for a crossing you have not walked yet.
cells.act: engage the hard part on purpose and see what holds
cells.ask: Go into the hard part you keep routing around — the conversation, the application, the turn — and stay in it long enough to see what holds when you're there.
cells.core:
The explanations have gotten sharper than the road. You can describe how it should go in more detail than the ground it crosses, and the plan is doing the work a walk is supposed to do. Sharp, no contact. The pressure is that nobody, including you, has put a foot on it.

Go stand in the hard part. One piece of it, the turn that keeps getting routed around: name it, face it, hold it, without a script. Contact will tell you fast whether the way is real or was only a good description — cheaper than another month of instructions.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door you already went through, still holding it open.
cells.act: return the small thing you owe before anyone asks
cells.ask: Hand back what you owe someone — a reply, a borrowed item, twenty promised minutes — early, before they bring it up, and say nothing about paying.
cells.core:
You know how it should go for other people; that part works. Where you are, the passage isn't opening — you can see the crossing and you're not on it, on the near bank as if the water were the same water. An old sense of an account left open keeps your feet where they are.

Don't force the feeling of being underway. Settle an account. A message owed back, a thing you borrowed, a stretch of time you said you'd give — return it before anyone asks, quietly, no announcement. That's the whole act. Fairness doesn't need a speech. Doing one owed thing settles the ground enough to take the next step.

cells.tense: You are steering with a steady hand and no memory of having taken the wheel.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Ask someone to carry a piece of the work alongside you, both names on it, and let your read of the route meet theirs without either of you shutting the other down.
cells.core:
The assurance others get from you didn't come from nowhere, and it isn't borrowed. You'd say you're just keeping things practical, and meanwhile the guidance is running, it's being followed, and your name isn't on it. You'd call it habit; the ones asking can tell the difference — they're asking because they can.

Being what you are doesn't take shape alone. It lands when one other person can see it with you. So take a piece of the work and ask someone to carry it alongside you — not to hand over, to join — and let their read of the route meet yours. When someone sees the direction moving through you, it stops being the ground you walk on and starts being yours.
